title_en: The subtle body, compared — Trika's two eights and Vedānta's 17/19
answer: Two systems, four inventories, and one warning that the number eight is not a shared unit. In Trika, Abhinavagupta gives the puryaṣṭaka ("city of eight") in two different ways — a prāṇa-based formula (five vital breaths + the two sense-organ groups + the inner organ = 8; expanded 18) and a tanmātra-based formula (five tanmātras + manas + buddhi + ahaṃkāra = 8) — and says the difference is in the formulation, not in the thing. In Advaita Vedānta the subtle body has 17 parts (5 prāṇas + 5 jñānendriyas + 5 karmendriyas + manas + buddhi) or 19 (adding ahaṃkāra and citta). The formal model below machine-checks the arithmetic and the non-identity of the partitions; it does not decide which inventory is metaphysically correct.

matrix.note: Counts are arithmetic identities inside the stipulated model. 'Expanded' means the inner organ is counted as its sub-faculties. The systems overlap in components; they do not share one partition.

claims.claim: Abhinavagupta distinguishes two eightfold formulas for the puryaṣṭaka and says the difference lies in the formulation (pakṣa), not in the thing (vastu).

evidence.label: ĪPVV — the prāṇa formula
evidence.quote_iast: prāṇādipañcakamindriyavargau dau niścayātmikā ca tṛtīyā svīkṛtāntaḥkaraṇāntarā dhīrvyajyate
evidence.quote_en: the five beginning with prāṇa, the two sense-organ groups, and the third, the determining inner organ — thus is the puryaṣṭaka expressed.
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim against the edition (the printed 'dau' is kept; read dvau). English is our gloss.

evidence.label: ĪPVV — the tanmātra formula and the reconciliation
evidence.quote_iast: tanmātrapañcakamantaḥkaraṇaṃ ceti kecana puryaṣṭakamāhuḥ sparśatanmātreṇa prāṇādisvīkārāt, tata eva atra pakṣavaicitrye vastuno na vaicitryam
evidence.quote_en: Some say the puryaṣṭaka is the five tanmātras together with the inner organ, since the breaths are subsumed under the tanmātra of touch; hence here the variety is in the formulation, not in the thing.
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim against the edition; English is our gloss.

claims.note: This is the key nuance: the two 'eights' are not rival realities in Abhinavagupta's own comment; they are two ways of stating one thing. The formal model checks that they are different partitions, not that one is false.

claims.claim: Formula A: five vital breaths + the two sense-organ groups + the inner organ = eight; expanded, eighteen.

evidence.label: ĪPVV (prāṇa formula)
evidence.quote_iast: prāṇādipañcakamindriyavargau dau niścayātmikā ca tṛtīyā svīkṛtāntaḥkaraṇāntarā dhīrvyajyate
evidence.quote_en: five prāṇas, two indriya groups, and the inner organ as the third — the city of eight.

claims.claim: Formula B: five tanmātras + manas + buddhi + ahaṃkāra = eight (Tantrāloka 24.19).

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 24.19
evidence.quote_iast: pūjayitvā śrutisparśau rasaṃ gandhaṃ vapurdvayam / dhyahaṃkṛtī manaśceti brahmādiṣvarpayetkramāt
evidence.quote_en: Having worshipped sound, touch, taste, smell, the two forms, the I-maker and mind, one offers them in order to Brahmā and the rest.
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim; English is our L2 (machine-proposed, UNREVIEWED). The list is compressed and does not spell out all eight names.

claims.claim: Medhananda's study corroborates the prāṇa-based formula; the primary witness is our ĪPVV passage above, not the monograph.

evidence.citation: Swami Medhananda, 'Abhinavagupta's Panentheism in Dialogue with Contemporary Neuroscience', in Göcke & Medhananda (eds), Panentheism in Indian and Western Thought (2023), ~p.13; citing Abhinavagupta 1985a 3:282 and Torella, ĪPK 2002, p.132 v.1.6.4.
evidence.quote_en: the subtle body, the City of Eight here includes the five vital breaths plus the two groups of sense organs
evidence.translation_note: Secondary corroboration (quoted briefly). The argument does not depend on it: the same formula is attested verbatim in ĪPVV chunkV3-M and bound to SubtleBody.lean.

claims.claim: Advaita Vedānta's subtle body has 17 components (5 prāṇas + 5 jñānendriyas + 5 karmendriyas + manas + buddhi) or 19 (adding ahaṃkāra and citta).

evidence.citation: Tattvabodha / Vedāntasāra (standard 17-part inventory); Maharaj (ed.), The Bloomsbury Research Handbook of Vedānta (2020), Śaṅkara chapter n.4 (subtle body: karmendriyas, jñānendriyas, prāṇas, mind).
evidence.quote_en: five organs of action, five organs of perception, physiological functions, and the mind
evidence.translation_note: External; not in our Sanskrit corpus and not re-verified here.

claims.claim: Vivekananda's liṅga/sūkṣmaśarīra bundles manas+buddhi, ahaṃkāra, indriyas and prāṇas; prāṇa is also used more widely for cosmic force.

evidence.citation: Swami Vivekananda, CW 2:456 and CW 2:438, as quoted in Swami Medhananda, Swami Vivekananda's Vedāntic Cosmopolitanism (2022), pp.317–318.
evidence.quote_en: The organs, the prāṇa functions, the mind and the buddhi combined, are called the finer body of man
evidence.translation_note: External; quoted briefly via Medhananda's study.

claims.claim: Prāṇa is not one definition across the systems: the count (five) is shared, the theoretical role is not.

evidence.citation: Formalised in trika-x formal-trika/control/SubtleBody.lean (prana_role_differs, prana_same_count_not_same_definition); sources: ĪPVV passage above; Bloomsbury Handbook n.4; Medhananda 2022 pp.317–318 (Rāja-Yoga cosmic force).
evidence.quote_en: same count, different role: vital breath vs physiological function vs cosmic force
evidence.translation_note: R-tier synthesis: the model records the stipulated roles; it does not adjudicate which use is metaphysically correct.

claims.note: This is the 'rigid definition' the comparison needs: prāṇa = (role, count), not a bare word. Two systems can agree on five and disagree on what a prāṇa is.

claims.claim: A third formulation appears in Śivasūtravimarśinī: five tanmātras + the three guṇas = eight, and this puryaṣṭaka is the subtle body and the cause of the gross.

evidence.label: Śivasūtravimarśinī (Kṣemarāja) — guṇa formula
evidence.quote_iast: tanmātrapañcakaṃ guṇatrayamiti sthūlaśarīrakāraṇabhūtamaṣṭakaṃ yat saṃniviṣṭaṃ tanmukhyaṃ puryaṣṭakaṃ
evidence.quote_en: the five tanmātras together with the three guṇas — that eightfold [thing] which is the cause of the gross body — that is the principal puryaṣṭaka.
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim. The text maps rajas→manas, tamas→ahaṃkāra, sattva→buddhi in the preceding words; the model does not identify the kinds, only their number.

claims.note: This is why 'eight' cannot be read off the word alone: three vocabularies, one count.

claims.claim: Tantrāloka 29 gives a three-level body schema — piṇḍa (para/kalātmā), the subtle puryaṣṭaka, and the outer gross body — and only the subtle one is carried.

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 29.261–270
evidence.quote_iast: piṇḍaḥ paraḥ kalātmā sūkṣmaḥ puryaṣṭako bahiḥ sthūlaḥ
evidence.quote_en: the piṇḍa is the supreme, the kalā-self; the subtle is the puryaṣṭaka; the gross is outside.

claims.note: Carried: the subtle body (Gītārthasaṅgraha on BG 15.8: the jīva departs 'puryaṣṭakena saha'; ŚSV: the gross is dropped). The model encodes exactly one carrier.

claims.claim: The formal model proves: all three formulas count eight, B and C differ in vocabulary though not count, A's kinds are disjoint from both, three body levels exist and exactly one is carried, and liberation drops ahaṃtā while keeping the units.

evidence.citation: trika-x formal-trika/control/SubtleBody.lean + SubtleBodyCorpus.lean: same_cardinality, partitions_disjoint, eight_is_not_one_eight, vedanta19_adds_citta, prana_role_differs; A_count, B_count, C_count, B_C_different_vocabulary, A_disjoint_B/C, guna_inner_same_count, three_levels, exactly_one_carried, liberation_drops_bodyness; run by control/run.sh with must-fail twins.
evidence.quote_en: three formulas, one count; three levels, one carrier
evidence.translation_note: Model-only: the theorems are about the stipulated decompositions, not about doctrine truth.

caveats: The counts are arithmetic inside the model; they are not evidence that a tradition 'really' has 8/17/19 parts.
Abhinavagupta's own reconciliation (pakṣavaicitrya) is quoted and bound, never proved.
Medhananda, the Bloomsbury Handbook and Vivekananda are external sources: cited, not re-verified here, and quoted only briefly.
The tanmātra list in TĀ 24.19 is compressed; the eightfold enumeration is R-tier reconstruction.
Our English for the Sanskrit witnesses is machine-proposed and UNREVIEWED unless a human signs it.
